name: Torgya at Tawang Monastery
when: January, from the 28th day of the 11th month of the Tibetan calendar (lunar); three days
summary: Torgya is Tawang Monastery's winter festival of masked cham dances, held over three days in January to drive away evil and bring good fortune for the coming year. Monpa families come in their finest clothes, and the courtyard fills from early morning.
body: Torgya is held in the main courtyard of Tawang Monastery, the largest monastery in India, over three days in the depth of winter. Monks in elaborate masks and silk robes perform cham dances that represent protective deities and animals, accompanied by long horns, drums and cymbals. The dances end with the burning of an effigy that carries the misfortunes of the past year, symbolically clearing the way for the new.

Dates follow the Tibetan lunar calendar and usually fall in January. Every third year, the larger Dungyur festival is held in place of Torgya, with the same spirit and even bigger crowds. Exact dates are announced by the monastery each year; check current status before you travel.

The festival is a religious event first. Monpa families from Tawang and surrounding villages come to watch, make offerings and receive blessings, and stalls sell food and goods around the monastery. Days are cold and clear, nights well below freezing, and hotels fill, so book early.
tips: Arrive in the courtyard by 8 am to find a place to sit; bring a cushion and a flask.
Ask about the monastery's rules on photography and never use flash during the dances.
Dress for sub-zero temperatures and book rooms at least two months ahead.

faqs.q: When is Torgya held at Tawang?
faqs.a: Usually in January, over three days from the 28th day of the 11th Tibetan month. Dates change each year with the lunar calendar. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can tourists watch the Torgya festival?
faqs.a: Yes. Visitors are welcome in the monastery courtyard. Dress modestly, sit where you are shown, and follow the monastery's rules on photography.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Torgya and Dungyur?
faqs.a: Torgya is the annual winter festival. Every third year the larger Dungyur festival is held in its place at Tawang Monastery, drawing even bigger crowds.

faqs.q: Is it very cold during Torgya?
faqs.a: Yes. Daytime temperatures in Tawang in January are around 0–8 °C, and nights fall well below freezing. Bring thermals, a down jacket, gloves and a warm hat.

name: Ziro Festival of Music
when: Late September, usually four days; dates announced each year
summary: Since 2012, the Ziro Festival of Music has brought independent musicians from northeast India and beyond to an outdoor stage among the Apatani paddies for four days each September. It is the best-known music festival in the region.
body: The festival is held in the Ziro valley, on open ground near the villages, with stages built largely of bamboo by local craftspeople. Lineups lean towards independent rock, folk, electronic and roots music, with strong representation from northeast Indian artists and some international acts. Days run into the night, and campers fill the valley.

It has also become a showcase for Apatani hospitality. Homestays across the valley host festival-goers, local food stalls serve rice, smoked meat and rice beer, and the organisers have encouraged waste reduction and reusable materials. Late September is the end of the monsoon, so expect some rain and muddy ground.

Passes, camping and dates are announced each year, usually a few months ahead. Accommodation and transport from Itanagar fill fast, so book early. Check current status before you travel, including ILP requirements for Lower Subansiri district.
tips: Book homestays and Sumo seats from Itanagar by June.
Pack waterproof boots, a rain jacket and warm layers for cold nights.
Carry cash; ATMs in Hapoli can run dry during the festival.

faqs.q: When is the Ziro Festival of Music?
faqs.a: Usually over four days in late September. Dates are announced each year by the organisers. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much does a Ziro Festival pass cost?
faqs.a: Four-day passes have cost a few thousand rupees in recent years, with camping extra. Prices change each year, so check the organisers' announcements.

faqs.q: Where can I stay for the Ziro Festival?
faqs.a: In festival campsites, Apatani homestays across the valley or a few hotels in Hapoli. Everything fills months ahead, so book by early summer.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for the Ziro Festival?
faqs.a: Yes. Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit for Lower Subansiri district, and foreigners a Protected Area Permit. Check current status before you travel.

name: Solung, the Adi harvest festival
summary: Solung is the most important festival of the Adi, held from 1 September across the Siang valley. Families make offerings for good crops and healthy livestock, women dance the ponung, and evenings bring song, feasting and apong rice beer.
body: Solung marks the end of the main sowing and weeding season. It begins on 1 September and lasts several days, with rituals that vary from village to village. Mithun and pigs may be sacrificed, offerings are made to deities of crops and animals, and families gather for feasts. Long ritual songs, sung by priests and elders, tell the origin of crops and of the Adi people.

The best-known public sight is the ponung, a dance in which young women move in a circle around a lead singer, who may hold a ritual sword. In Pasighat, public celebrations add cultural programmes to the village rituals, which makes it the easiest place for visitors to see Solung.

September is still the monsoon in the Siang valley, so roads can be affected. If you are invited to a village celebration, go with a local guide, ask before photographing rituals and accept apong politely. Check current status before you travel.
tips: Go with a local guide who can arrange an invitation to a village celebration.
Ask before photographing rituals and sacrifices, and accept a no.
Allow buffer days; monsoon rain can close roads in the Siang valley.

faqs.a: Solung begins on 1 September and lasts several days. Village programmes and public events in Pasighat vary each year; check current status before you travel.
The ponung is a dance performed by Adi women during Solung, moving in a circle around a lead singer who chants the songs of the festival.
Yes. Public celebrations in Pasighat are open, and with a local guide you may be invited to a village. Be respectful during rituals and ask before taking photos.

faqs.q: Where is the best place to see Solung?
faqs.a: Pasighat, for public celebrations, and the Adi villages around it with a guide. Aalo and other Siang valley towns also celebrate.
